title: International Court of Justice orders Israel to halt its Rafah offensive
body:
On 24 May 2024, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague issued a new order on provisional measures in the case brought by South Africa against Israel under the Genocide Convention. The court voted 13 to 2 to order Israel to immediately halt its military offensive and any other action in the Rafah Governorate that could bring about conditions of life for the Palestinian group in Gaza leading to its physical destruction in whole or in part.

The order also required Israel to keep the Rafah border crossing open for the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid, and to ensure unimpeded access to Gaza for any United Nations-mandated investigative or fact-finding body examining allegations of genocide. Israel was told to report to the court on its compliance within one month. The ruling followed a request South Africa submitted on 10 May 2024 and oral hearings held in the week before the decision.

The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. Its orders are legally binding, but the court has no direct means of enforcing them. The order addressed provisional measures only and did not rule on the merits of South Africa's claim that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, which Israel rejects. It was the third set of provisional measures in the case, after earlier orders in January and March 2024.
